A reusable broad phase
inside a live C++ physics demo
The first result is narrow but measurable: guarded candidate reuse reduced CPU step time in one deterministic XPBD cloth experiment.
Exploratory result · Apple M2 Pro · fixed scene and settings · no IPC / OGC adapter
Kyoto research discussion · Swayam Singal · 2 November 2026

This is a working research prototype and a bounded measurement, not a universal speedup claim. The comparison uses the same C++ XPBD cloth solver, SAP margin 0.05, displacement budget 0.04, fixed dt 1/120, and paired runs on an Apple M2 Pro. See benchmark slide and output/native/benchmark-summary.txt.
Can candidate generation be shared safely?
Many simulators repeatedly search for geometrically nearby primitives.
A common service could own conservative bounds, spatial search and stable pair output.
Bounds · eligibility · candidate pairs · reuse policy
Narrow phase · contact meaning · solver · tolerances
The proposal shares search infrastructure, not contact mathematics.

Research question: can a reusable geometric candidate-generation interface support different simulators without weakening method-specific correctness requirements? IPC, OGC, XPBD and CCFR retain distinct contact semantics and solver assumptions. CCFR is a collision-handling method compatible with XPBD, not an independent XPBD solver. Sources are provided in speaker notes on the method boundary slide.
The demo keeps the stages visible
Observed in one process: the C++ solver consumes the service’s candidate output.
Discrete sphere–triangle query · no self-collision · no CCD

This is a full same-process demonstration: an XPBD cloth solver calls the generic BroadPhaseService and uses returned candidate pairs for precise sphere-triangle proximity. The service provides stable candidates. This prototype has no continuous collision detection, cloth self-collision, IPC integration or OGC integration. The GUI reports frame, candidate, proximity, CPU step and broad-phase timing.
A small contract carries the caller’s query meaning

A stable, deduplicated list of candidate ID pairs
Precise tests decide contact; the broad phase does not.

Implemented record: Bounds{id,min,max,category,mask,movable}; QueryRequest{margin,displacementBudget,updatePolicy}. The service expands each bound by half the requested margin. Candidate output is an actual pair list, not only a count. Downstream narrow phase decides precise contact. Caller controls geometry and semantics; current demo supports sphere-triangle proximity.

Bᵢ(t): padded current bound · Eᵢ: stored envelope · unchanged IDs, masks, request and backend

alt: Typeset set inclusion certificate: current padded box overlaps are a subset of cached guarded-envelope overlaps

text: Certificate: if each current padded bound B_i(t) is contained by its stored envelope E_i, then any pair of current padded bounds that overlap is also a pair of overlapping envelopes. The cached pair list is built from envelope overlaps. Reuse requires unchanged primitive IDs, eligibility masks, query request (including margin/budget/policy) and broad-phase backend. The certificate concerns discrete query bounds at evaluation time; it does not certify the continuous path between steps. In the measured run, margin was 0.05 and displacement budget 0.04.

Measured CPU step time fell in this paired run
5 paired trials · 1,350 measured steps / policy · Apple M2 Pro · Release
CPU timing includes the oracle and excludes rendering · exploratory single-scene result

alt: CPU step time chart showing mean p95 and maximum across rebuild and guarded reuse policies

text: Source: output/native/benchmark-summary.txt and output/native/benchmark.png, generated from output/native/live_benchmark.csv. Mean/max/p95 (ms): rebuild 2.35117 / 4.18375 / 2.72708; guarded reuse 0.999491 / 2.9505 / 1.19762. The experiment ran Release C++ on Apple M2 Pro, same-process XPBD cloth, sweep-and-prune, margin 0.05, displacement budget 0.04, dt 1/120. Five paired trials of 300 steps per policy; first 30 steps of each trial warmed up, leaving 1,350 measured steps per policy. CPU step time is wall-clock CPU-side timing and excludes rendering. Results are exploratory for this implementation and machine; do not generalize to other geometries or simulators.
The time reduction tracks fewer broad-phase rebuilds
Maximum position error: 0 across measured trajectories
2,700 measured CSV rows · 1,350 steps per policy · 5 trials per policy

Benchmark summary reports generatorCalls 12150 versus 600 and 11550 reuses, with maxPositionError 0 and measuredFramesPerPolicy 1350. The 2700-row CSV contains measured rows for both policies and excludes warmup. The native capture trace checks at frame 120 also have matching state hashes and zero oracle misses. These checks apply to this tested scene/configuration only and do not establish general equivalence for other methods.

Literature measurement anchors retained from the proposal: IPC, Fig. 23 and Table 1 (https://ipc-sim.github.io/file/IPC-paper-fullRes.pdf); OGC, Figs. 17–18, Table 1 and §5 (https://graphics.cs.utah.edu/research/projects/ogc/Offset_Geometric_Contact-SIGGRAPH2025.pdf); CCFR, Table 1 and Figs. 10–11 (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26901v1). These inform future evaluation design only. They are not measurements of this demo. CCFR is compatible with XPBD but has its own collision-free-region formulation.

This experiment tests an infrastructure seam, not solver interchangeability.

CCFR: Kikuchi and Kanai, “Convex Collision-Free Regions,” arXiv:2607.26901 (2026). It constructs local convex feasible regions for non-penetration and is compatible with XPBD, while remaining a distinct collision handling method. The prototype does not reproduce CCFR, IPC, or OGC and does not claim their guarantees. Official research project links: IPC https://ipc-sim.github.io/ ; OGC https://ankachan.github.io/Projects/OGC/ ; XPBD source https://github.com/InteractiveComputerGraphics/PositionBasedDynamics .
The next test should change one method boundary
Select one existing solver and one representative scene.
Replace only candidate generation with the shared service.
Compare pair coverage, collision outcomes and measured cost.
Which method and correctness requirement should anchor that adapter?

Discussion objective: agree on the first external adapter and its correctness oracle. Preserve the method’s own narrow phase, tolerances, solver and acceptance tests. The prototype demonstrates one seam in an XPBD cloth implementation; it does not yet prove reuse across heterogeneous simulators.
